title: unified-rollouts-enhanced-autorollback-multi-metric-shadow-canary-ab
author: Ethan Miller
description: Motivation: Improve safety and observability for unified rollouts by extending the automatic rollback policy to support multi-metric decisioning and better handling of shadow and AB/canary traffic. This PR introduces a declarative multi-metric policy that lets users express weighted metric thresholds, noise-tolerant windows, and explicit metric mapping for shadow traffic. It also centralizes decision logic in the rollouts controller so canary and AB flows share the same evaluation paths. Changes include controller and policy logic, new e2e tests, and docs. Checklist: - Implement multi-metric policy and evaluation engine - Wire policy into unified rollouts controller - Add metric smoothing and noise-tolerant windowing - Add integration for shadow traffic metric mapping - Add e2e tests for canary/AB/shadow rollback scenarios - Update rollout docs and migration notes Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged unless a new multi-metric policy is configured; old single-metric policies still supported. Related: ENG-4821 (multi-metric autodecision), ENG-4873 (shadow traffic metric mapping), SUP-912 (customer incident that motivated stricter rollback windows).
commits: feat(rollouts): add multi-metric auto-rollback policy | feat(controller): plumb multi-metric evaluation into unified controller | fix(metrics): tolerate missing metric series in shadow mode | test(e2e): add canary/ab/shadow rollback scenarios | docs(rollouts): document policy schema and migration notes
conversation: Priya Kapoor: Can you clarify how the weighted thresholds interact with the existing SLO-driven heuristics? The current implementation looks additive and could mask latency regressions.
Ethan Miller: The weights are normalized and applied after SLO heuristics. We added an explicit SLO-exempt flag so SLO regressions always override weights — added tests to cover this case.
Marisol Garcia: Unit tests look good. Two nits on naming in multi_metric_policy.go (suggest clearer method names).
Ethan Miller: Addressed naming nits and pushed an additional commit. Updated comment blocks to explain evaluation order.
Liam Chen: CI flaky test in e2e showed up once, restarted pipeline. After rerun, all checks passed. Approved.
merge_commit_summary: squash: unified rollouts: multi-metric auto-rollback and shadow mapping
release_notes: Added multi-metric automatic rollback policy for unified rollouts with weighted thresholds and noise-tolerant windows. Shadow traffic metric mapping is supported. Backwards compatible by default.
notes_on_migration: Existing single-metric policies continue to work. To migrate to multi-metric policies, translate previous single-metric threshold into a single-entry weights array and validate in staging. New policy schema documented in docs/rollouts.md.
e2e_results_summary: Added new e2e scenarios covering: progressive canary with latency/accuracy dual metrics, shadow traffic mapping and rollback triggering, and AB-test variant mismatch. All scenarios pass in CI cluster after stabilization retries.
related_incidents: SUP-912: customer reported noisy metric spikes during a shadow rollout that didn't trigger rollback; this PR tightens windows and mapping to prevent recurrence.
qa_notes: QA should exercise canary/AB/shadow combinations with synthetic metric generators. Watch for false positives; use the noise-tolerance window config to tune.
